scenarios.label: Large miss toward R (R+6; 2020 was R+8)

sources.national_sd: SD of cycle-level governor poll bias 3.1 (3.4 since 2010); governor and Senate cycle biases correlate 0.88 (538 raw_polls recompute 1998-2024)
sources.regional_sd: Census-region clustering near zero (implied ~0.5); 1.25 kept to cover demographic misses like 2020
sources.state_sd: Residual race error after removing cycle bias: 4.05 for competitive races with 4+ polls, 3.7 with 11+
sources.single_poll_sd: Individual governor polls scatter 4.43 around their race mean
sources.per_undecided: Absolute error rises ~0.09 per undecided point (r = 0.20)
sources.fundamentals_sd: Fitted presidential-lean + swing residual in competitive races since 2012: 9.2-10.3; 11 used
sources.pres_lean_coef: Presidential-margin coefficient for governor margins 0.73-0.83 in competitive races since 2012 (vs ~0.8-1 for Senate)
sources.national_shift_factor: Fitted national-swing coefficient for governors 0.37-0.62, vs 0.66-0.80 for Senate
sources.incumbency_bonus: Regression estimates 10-12 (8 in competitive races), shaded for selection bias (weak incumbents retire)
sources.last_gov_weight: Adding the previous governor margin barely improves the fit (SD 14.0 -> 13.8), so it gets 20%
sources.partisan_shift: Sponsored governor polls lean 3.9-4.3 toward the sponsor (n = 137-244)
sources.lean_shift: Judgment: unsponsored one-party pollsters, roughly half the sponsored effect
sources.prior_bias: Zero: governor poll bias has leaned D on average (+1.1 to +2.1) but its sign does not persist (lag-1 r ~ 0); tested as scenarios
sources.t_df: State errors mildly fat-tailed (implied df ~13); 6 used because of 2020's +8.3 national miss
sources.independent_extra_sd: Judgment: thin record for independent-vs-R races
